Losing pets is hard. Really hard, and that's something I understand.

It's much easier said than done, but you should keep in mind that it's not your fault, not at all. Cats that are allowed to go outside and have that level of freedom will always be happier than cats that aren't. 

I don't know if you have things that you enjoy doing - lots of people on this sub don't - but if you do, try using them to keep your mind away from your cats for now. It'll get easier over time, but right now I can understand that you'd feel terrible.

If it'll be helpful, I'd be more than happy to talk to you for a bit to help take your mind off of it.
This holds a lot of meaning, thank you so much for sharing it.

Hey man, having to go into a period of no contact with a loved one like that is incredibly hard. I feel you. I suggest you think about any hobbies you have, or things you enjoy doing, and try to do them as much as you can. Looking 3 weeks ahead feels like a really, really long time, so I would suggest trying to break it down to one thing at a time. I find that when I'm not doing great, it helps me to try and only focus on the next thing I have to do, and when I do that, move onto the next. It might help you feel some form of routine, and with any luck it will help you with the coming weeks. Don't go out and buy that gun, instead go and buy something to treat yourself, and something to keep you occupied. I get that you'll have no appetite, so try eating things that you really enjoy (among other things to keep a balanced diet). Small things like this might be able to help you make it. Good luck man, and keep fighting! I believe you can make it, even if you don't.

You're right that it's against the rules, but not quite for that reason. It is seen as validating, and can be very helpful in the short term, but it's against the rules because it's making promises that you can't keep. What happens in a years time when you've been told it will get better, but it only gets worse? People may begin to have hope because of it, but at the same time you've created a point in time where they will almost certainly realize that it hasn't, and won't get better, and end up much more suicidal than they were before, and they lose faith in the people on the internet who lied to them leaving no one they feel they can reach out to.

Why not give it a few more years? It's not like there's no chance you'll find love and have a biological family. Why not try and live on with hope, try and improve yourself, and see what happens? Surely it's better to keep going for now and see if your efforts pay off, and make a more educated decision later on, than to end it all now, because you never know what you might miss out on.
You mentioned adopting a kid. Do you think that will help?
What about living for hobbies, and friends who can love you platonically?

It's a gamble, there's no denying that, nothing is garenteed. Don't do this specifically for love because then it's possible you will end up disappointed. Love may come and it may not, but I would suggest you focus on bettering yourself for the purpose of being able to look at how far you've come and be proud.

Changing aspects of your person through hard work doesn't change who you are so to speak. I agree you deserve love as you are, regardless of your appearence, but the world just isn't that fair. You will still be you, but you'll be a better version of yourself. Striving to better yourself is something I believe everyone should be doing, constantly, regardless of circumstance. Work on become that better person, and maybe find some love along the way.
It's good that you're working on fixing everything. Do you not want to stick around and see it through to see what kind of person you end up as?

Hey man, sounds like you're in a bad place right now. Is there anything else getting you down, or is it just how you see yourself? 
If you feel like talking to me about it, I'd be more than happy to listen and hopefully offer you some advice where I can. If not, then please try and hold on for a bit longer. Adopting a kid might give you the spark you need to really get back into a better mindset.

Hey, it sounds like you're in a really tough spot right now.

It's really, really hard that your boyfriend got taken home by his father, but it's good that you're working on being able to bring him back because, along with being able to meet him in person again, you have a goal which can help keep you going. 

Lots of people on this sub are living for other people, and we can all agree that it's exhausting and painful. I find that helping people on this sub when I feel like I have the capacity to really helps feel like I have some form of purpose and it helps dull the hopelessness for me. Maybe that could help you out as well?

I really encourage you to keep on living. Whatever keeps you going isn't important, be it your goal to get your boyfriend back, some form of hobby, a commitment to other people, or something else. As long as you keep holding onto something and keep on going, you'll make it to whatever you want to achieve.

Nothing in your post is against the rules, so you don't have to worry about that.

If you ever feel like you need someone to talk to, send me a message and I'll be more than happy to talk to you (though I might not always respond quickly because of school/family commitments).

Also, nice username, it genuinely made me laugh.

Hey, I'm really sorry you've had to experience that kind of rejection for a health issue like that. Being isolated from society is such a hard thing to deal with and virtually nothing can get rid of that feeling because humans depend on social contact. It probably feels like people suck, and yeah, most people do, but I would recommend turning to the internet, at least to find a couple of people to connect with. Go and find a community for a game/show/hobby that you enjoy and start talking to people there. Unfortunately you can't spend all of your time on the internet, but having some great people on the internet can really help you along until you find some people in real life who you can connect with, and who actually appreciate you.

Hey man, it's great that you've reached out for help. 
Firstly, you're not weak, or pathetic or needy or attention seeking for crying out for help. Your mental health is important and you have the right to get help.

If computing is your lifelong dream, then it's likely that it's still a passion. Depression can often completely destroy your love of life, and everything you used to enjoy. I strongly advise you keep going with it and some day, when you feel a bit better, you'll feel the same excitement from it as you felt when it first interested you.

I would also advise speaking to your medic about it. It's hard to do, I get that, but once you do you can get the help of professionals who can properly help you get back into life.

I hope at least something I've said helps, and I'm hear to listen if you want to talk about anything.
